# Larkmoor Comfort Heating & Air - Company Profile

Prepared by Dana Pruitt for the owners, updated October 2026. Reporting year: November 1, 2025 to October 31, 2026.

## History

Glen Vossberg started Larkmoor Comfort in 1994 after twelve years as a service technician for another contractor. He worked out of his garage with one van. His wife Ruth Vossberg ran the books and the phone from the kitchen table. The company moved to its current building at 2290 Fenwick Road, Larkmoor, Ohio in 2003. The building has the office, a small warehouse with a parts cage, and parking for the fleet.

Their son Kyle Vossberg joined in 2011 as a service technician and became operations manager in 2019. Glen is still president and still signs every equipment purchase over $10,000 and every commercial contract. Ruth is vice president and handles payroll and HR.

## What we do

Residential service and repair: furnaces, heat pumps, central air conditioners, ductless mini-splits, humidifiers, thermostats. Standard service call (diagnostic) fee is $99. Average residential repair ticket is about $410.

Residential system replacement: a Comfort Advisor (Nadia Ferris) visits, measures and gives a written proposal with three options. Typical installed price is $9,500 to $16,000 for a furnace and air conditioner. Average install ticket is about $11,800. We sell mostly Aerovance equipment, bought through Northgate Supply.

Comfort Club maintenance plan: $189 per year, two tune-ups (spring cooling, fall heating), priority scheduling, no overtime charge, 15% off repairs. 640 members at the snapshot.

Commercial: preventive maintenance (PM) agreements with about 90 building owners and property managers (offices, retail strips, churches, two private schools). Agreements are one year, usually 2 to 4 visits per year. Commercial PM revenue is about $410,000 a year. We also replace rooftop units (RTUs), about 40 per year.

## Volumes for the reporting year

- Service calls (residential and commercial repair): about 5,200
- Comfort Club tune-ups scheduled: 1,280 (640 members x 2)
- Residential installs: 310
- Commercial RTU replacements: 40
- Commercial PM visits: about 290 across 90 agreements
- After-hours messages from the answering service: about 1,050
- Website request forms: about 410

## Revenue and size

Revenue for the reporting year is about $6.4 million: residential service and repair about $2.1 million, residential replacement about $3.4 million (310 installs at about $11,800 average is $3.66 million gross, less some financing fees and adjustments), commercial about $0.8 million, Comfort Club about $121,000. Equipment purchases from Northgate Supply are about $1.2 million a year.

We have 35 employees: 11 in the office and 24 in the field (14 service technicians, 8 installers, 2 apprentices). We run 16 service vans and 3 install trucks.

## Customers and area

Mostly homeowners in Larkmoor, Westerville, Gahanna, New Albany, Delaware and the north and east Columbus suburbs. About 70% of residential customers have used us before. Commercial customers are mostly local property managers; the largest is Brookfield Pike Properties with 14 buildings under agreement.

## Main suppliers

- Northgate Supply (Columbus branch): Aerovance equipment, coils, most parts. We have bought from them since 1994.
- Ridgeview HVAC Supply: filters and some parts when Northgate is out.
- Buckeye Sheet Metal: custom ductwork and transitions.
- Fleet fuel cards, uniforms and the answering service (Midstate Answering) are the other regular vendors.

document_chunks.text: External context only, gathered October 2026. These are published industry figures from vendor blogs and trade press, not facts about any one company. Vendor sources sell software and may lean optimistic.

document_chunks.name: research/01_staffing_tools_and_economics.md
document_chunks.heading: Revenue per technician and margins
document_chunks.text:
A 2026 contractor benchmark roundup puts revenue per service technician at roughly $150,000 to $250,000 a year and industry-average net margin at 5% to 12%, with top-quartile firms at 15% to 25%. Source: https://simprogroup.com/blog/hvac-industry-statistics-2026

Other vendor guides put the average net margin around 8% to 12% and a healthy gross margin near 50% to 55%. Source: https://www.housecallpro.com/learn/guide-to-hvac-profits-salaries-revenue/

document_chunks.name: research/01_staffing_tools_and_economics.md
document_chunks.heading: Tools in use
document_chunks.text:
A Verizon Connect survey cited by BuildOps found about 51% of field service companies use field service management software, about 25% still use spreadsheets, and the rest rely on whiteboards and other manual methods. Source: https://buildops.com/manual-processes-to-field-service-management-software

A 2026 Salesforce field service survey of about 2,300 professionals found 52% still use spreadsheets and 43% still rely on paper logs for field assets. Source: https://www.salesforce.com/service/resources/state-of-field-service-report/

document_chunks.name: research/01_staffing_tools_and_economics.md
document_chunks.heading: Limits
document_chunks.text: Most figures come from software vendors and mix company sizes. Small family firms with 20 to 50 staff are often not separated out. Treat the ranges as rough context.

document_chunks.name: research/02_maintenance_agreements_and_renewals.md
document_chunks.heading: Renewal benchmarks
document_chunks.text:
Contracting Business, an HVAC trade publication, recommends at least an 86% annual renewal rate for maintenance agreements. Source: https://www.contractingbusiness.com/residential-hvac/article/20868670/hvac-maintenance-agreements-by-the-numbers

Vendor guides commonly cite a 70% to 80% renewal target, with strong programs near 90%. Source: https://oxmaint.com/industries/hvac/hvac-service-contract-renewal-retention-tracking

ACHR News profiled a Pennsylvania contractor with about 1,600 agreements and an 83% renewal rate. Source: https://www.achrnews.com/articles/153291-contractors-share-maintenance-agreement-best-practices

document_chunks.name: research/02_maintenance_agreements_and_renewals.md
document_chunks.heading: Why agreements lapse
document_chunks.text: Several vendor sources say renewals slip when reminders depend on someone running a manual export or remembering to call, and suggest scheduled reminders by text, email and phone. These claims come from companies selling automation and their lift figures are not independently verified.

document_chunks.name: research/02_maintenance_agreements_and_renewals.md
document_chunks.heading: Scope benchmarks
document_chunks.text: Residential plans usually include two visits a year; commercial plans often four, guided by the ACCA Standard 4 maintenance scope. Source: https://www.smartservice.com/blog/how-much-hvac-service-agreements

document_chunks.name: research/02_maintenance_agreements_and_renewals.md
document_chunks.heading: Limits
document_chunks.text: Renewal figures vary by residential versus commercial and by how a firm counts auto-renewing card plans.

scored_opportunities.name: Omni-Channel Dispatch Consolidator
scored_opportunities.what_the_agent_does: Ingests service requests from phone, web forms, social media, and answering service emails; deduplicates entries, auto-prioritizes by urgency, and pushes clean records to the central dispatch spreadsheet.
scored_opportunities.gap: Manual data entry across overlapping channels creates duplicate rows and delayed callbacks.
scored_opportunities.rating_reason: High value by eliminating duplicate rows and callback delays; moderate effort to integrate channel APIs; low risk as it only routes operational data.

scored_opportunities.name: Paper-to-QuickBooks Auto-Inker
scored_opportunities.what_the_agent_does: Uses OCR to read three-part paper tickets, extracts labor and part numbers, matches against dispatch status, and drafts QuickBooks commercial invoices.
scored_opportunities.gap: Illegible handwriting and missing part numbers on yellow tickets delay commercial invoicing by ~8 days.
scored_opportunities.rating_reason: High value by cutting invoicing time and reducing missing tickets; moderate-high effort due to OCR variability and QuickBooks API mapping; medium risk requires human review of financial outputs.

scored_opportunities.name: Contract Renewal & Tune-Up Scheduler
scored_opportunities.what_the_agent_does: Tracks Comfort Club and PM contract status, auto-schedules seasonal tune-ups based on expiration dates, and triggers renewal outreach emails.
scored_opportunities.gap: Paper-based renewal process and missed season-end outreach lead to skipped bookings.
scored_opportunities.rating_reason: Solid value by preventing missed visits and lapsed agreements; low effort using existing contract data; low risk as it only schedules appointments and sends notifications.

scored_opportunities.name: Commissioning & Warranty Compliance Checker
scored_opportunities.what_the_agent_does: Automatically assembles written proposals from site-survey data and verifies that each installation record contains required commissioning readings before closeout.
scored_opportunities.gap: Failed inspections and 30-day callbacks due to missing commissioning data or permit delays.
scored_opportunities.rating_reason: High value by reducing callbacks and failed inspections; moderate effort to parse survey data and permit logs; medium risk requires human verification of technical readings.

scored_opportunities.name: Smart PO Router & Stock Predictor
scored_opportunities.what_the_agent_does: Routes purchase orders to approvers based on predefined thresholds, predicts van stock depletion using historical usage, and flags out-of-stock items for alternative sourcing.
scored_opportunities.gap: Approver unavailability and frequent out-of-stock items cause delivery delays and extra supplier trips.
scored_opportunities.rating_reason: Strong value by keeping projects moving and reducing supplier trips; moderate effort to integrate supplier APIs and approval workflows; low risk as it only suggests orders for human confirmation.

scored_opportunities.name: QuickBooks Reconciliation & Data Cleaner
scored_opportunities.what_the_agent_does: Continuously aligns spreadsheet data with QuickBooks, flags Northgate statement discrepancies, and compiles the Monthly Numbers workbook for leadership review.
scored_opportunities.gap: Manual data cleaning and misaligned spreadsheets delay financial close when bookkeeper is absent.
scored_opportunities.rating_reason: High value by enabling timely close and accurate reporting; high effort due to complex mapping and reconciliation logic; medium-high risk requires strict human review, governance tracking, and off/recovery switches as foundation work.

scored_opportunities.what_the_agent_does: Greets visitors and offers starting choices (Schedule a Comfort Club; Request Emergency Service; Get a System Quote), answers common questions from approved business information, and hands off to a person.

roadmaps.rationale: Starting with the Paper-to-QuickBooks Auto-Inker addresses the highest-value bottleneck by automating invoice drafting, which immediately improves cash flow and reduces manual data entry errors. Following this with the Omni-Channel Dispatch Consolidator streamlines incoming service requests, ensuring dispatchers have clean, prioritized data to act upon without double-booking or missing calls. Finally, implementing the Contract Renewal & Tune-Up Scheduler locks in recurring revenue by automating outreach, which naturally follows once intake and billing workflows are stabilized.
roadmaps.pilot_reason: The first idea serves as the pilot because it directly tackles the most time-consuming manual process with proven technology, delivering immediate measurable value and building team confidence before expanding to multi-channel intake automation.
roadmaps.assumption: This plan assumes that the existing paper service tickets are consistently legible and standardized enough for software to accurately extract labor and part numbers without excessive manual correction.

rubric.objection: While the value is high, relying on OCR for paper tickets introduces a potential point of failure that needs careful consideration and fallback plans.

roadmaps.rationale: Beginning with the lowest-effort maintenance scheduler quickly generates recurring revenue and strengthens customer retention without demanding significant technical resources. This order maximizes early wins and builds operational confidence before tackling more complex data integration.
